extracted.intended_audience: Applicants for NRC licenses (facility, material, waste disposal), their representatives, and NRC staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and requirements for filing, tendering, docketing, distributing, and administratively reviewing NRC license applications (including special rules for multi-part submissions, HLW repositories, and part 61 waste licenses), and for issuing notices of hearing and actions on applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Portable storage media
rubrics_metrics.description: Portable storage media means a physical piece of hardware that can be added to and removed from a computing device or network for the purpose of transferring or storing electronic files. Examples include optical media (CDs, DVDs) and non-optical media (SSDs, flash drives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Potential party
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential party means any person who has requested, or who may intend to request, a hearing or petition to intervene in a hearing under 10 CFR part 2, other than hearings conducted under Subparts J and M of 10 CFR part 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Presiding officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer means the Commission, an administrative law judge, an administrative judge, an Atomic Safety and Licensing Board, or other person designated in accordance with the provisions of this part, presiding over the conduct of a hearing conducted under the provisions of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Public Document Room
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Document Room means the facility at the NRC at which agency public records will ordinarily be made available for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Safeguards Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Safeguards Information means information (not classified as National Security Information or Restricted Data) that specifically identifies detailed control and accounting procedures, detailed security measures, security measures for physical protection and location of certain plant equipment vital to safety, and other information within scope of Section 147 of the Atomic Energy Act, the unauthorized disclosure of which could reasonably be expected to have a significant adverse effect on public health and safety or common defense and security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary means the Secretary to the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to file an application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a permit, license, license transfer, license amendment, license renewal, or a standard design approval must be filed with the Director, Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation, or the Director, Office of Nuclear Material Safety and Safeguards, as prescribed by the applicable provisions of this chapter. A prospective applicant may confer informally with NRC staff before filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the appropriate Director based on the subject matter of the application; informal pre-filing conferences are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendered application process and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine whether an application is complete and acceptable for docketing it will initially be treated as a tendered application; a copy of the tendered application will be available for public inspection on the NRC website and/or at the NRC Public Document Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination on acceptability for docketing is generally made within 30 days; in selected cases the Commission may determine acceptability based on technical adequacy and extend the determination period (generally to 60 days) while issuing a notice of hearing as soon as practicable under §2.104(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of docket number and post-tender requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director determines the tendered application (or portion) is complete and acceptable for docketing, a docket number will be assigned and the applicant will be notified and requested to submit additional copies and take specified distribution actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested actions include submitting additional copies required by applicable regulations, serving copies and notices on chief executives, making direct distribution to Federal/State/local officials per written instructions, and submitting an affidavit listing names and addresses of served officials. Do not publicly distribute parts subject to §2.390(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required in notice of availability served on chief executives
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of availability served on the chief executive must contain: the docket number; a brief description of the proposed site and facility; the location of the site and facility as primarily proposed and alternatively listed; contact name, address, telephone number, and email of applicant's representative; notification that a draft environmental impact statement will be issued and available upon request; and notification that upon request the applicant will transmit a copy of the application and environmental report (and changes affecting alternative site location).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must submit an affidavit that service of the notice has been completed along with a list of names and addresses of those executives upon whom the notice was served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution format and completeness of distributed copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies submitted to, and distributed by, the applicant shall be completely assembled documents, identified by docket number. Subsequently distributed amendments may consist of revised pages; recipients are responsible for inserting revised pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tendered application will be formally docketed upon receipt of the required additional copies; distribution is deemed complete when copies are deposited in the mail or with a carrier prepaid for delivery to designated addresses; date of docketing is when required copies are received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of distribution after docketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days after docketing, the applicant must submit to the appropriate Director an affidavit (or written statement) that distribution of the additional copies to Federal, State, Tribal, and local officials has been completed in accordance with the chapter's requirements and written instructions furnished by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit must accompany a list of names and addresses of officials upon whom the notice or copies were served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of incomplete tendered applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a tendered application (or part) is determined to be incomplete and not acceptable for processing, the applicant will be informed of the determination and the respects in which the document is deficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director will specify deficiencies; determinations of completeness are generally made within 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-part submission option and timing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain applicants (construction permit under part 50 or 53, combined license under part 52 or 53, testing facility, or applicants subject to §51.20(b)) may submit required information in two parts; one part must be accompanied by specified information and the other part includes remaining information. One part may precede or follow the other by no longer than 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If either part is incomplete the Director will inform the applicant of deficiencies and completeness will generally be determined within 30 days. The first-filed part must include required fees and enumerated regulatory information (see referenced sections). Additional parts are docketed upon determination of completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-part submission for early site suitability consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant seeking early review/hearing and early partial decision on site suitability may submit information in three parts. Part one must include the information relating to site suitability and certain baseline application sections; part one must include proposed findings on site suitability, a range of postulated design/operation parameters sufficient for review, and information on site selection process and long-range development plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part two and part three must include the remaining required information (specified statutory/regulatory sections) and must be submitted during the period the partial decision on part one is effective; submission of part two and part three must be no more than 6 months apart (one may precede/follow the other by up to 6 months). Separate parallel rules apply for combined license under part 52 (with specific cross-references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special procedures for HLW repository applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for construction authorization or licenses for HLW repositories (parts 60 or 63) and related EIS documents are processed under special paragraph (e) procedures: treated as tendered documents for completeness determination, copies available for public inspection in the PDR, and twenty copies must be filed to enable completeness determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If acceptable for docketing, additional copies are requested and distribution/affidavit/docketing rules apply as for other applications; the Director will publish notice of docketing in the Federal Register identifying State/location and give notice to the governor; the notice will state that a hearing is required in the public interest prior to issuance of a construction authorization and recite matters in §2.104(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 61 (low-level radioactive waste disposal) special processing and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for licenses under part 61 and accompanying environmental reports are treated as tendered documents; one original and two copies shall be filed to enable determination of completeness; the Commission will publish Federal Register notice of the filed application and notify governors, legislatures, other State/county/municipal officials, and Tribal governing bodies of affected areas; the Commission will post public notice in newspapers of general circulation summarizing the tendered application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When tendered document is complete and acceptable a docket number will be assigned; applicant will be requested to submit additional copies, serve chief executives, make direct distribution to officials, and serve notice of availability. Distribution rules, affidavit requirements, and formal docketing upon receipt of required additional copies apply. The Commission will publish a notice under §2.105 offering opportunity to request a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative review: staff requests and review schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: During staff review, the applicant may be required to supply additional information. The staff may require any party to confer informally. For docketed applications for specified authorizations, the NRC staff shall establish a schedule for its review specifying key intermediate steps from docketing until completion of review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to respond to information requests and participate in informal conferences; ensure readiness to meet the review schedule established by staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACRS referral and record inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will refer docketed applications to the Advisory Committee on Reactor Safeguards (ACRS) as required by law or as otherwise appropriate; ACRS will render reports to the Commission, which will be made part of the record and transmitted to appropriate State and local officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should anticipate ACRS involvement where required and that ACRS reports become part of the administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action on applications: issuance when compliant
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appropriate Director finds an application for byproduct, source, special nuclear material, facility, or operator license complies with the requirements of the Act, the Energy Reorganization Act, and this chapter, the Director will issue a license and will inform State, Tribal and local officials specified in §2.104(c) of the issuance for certain categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice-of-issuance requirements for licenses under part 61 are addressed separately in §2.106(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Action on applications: proposed denial and applicant rights
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appropriate Director finds an application does not comply with the Act and this chapter, the Director may issue a notice of proposed denial or a notice of denial, and must inform the applicant in writing of: (1) the nature of any deficiencies or the reason for the proposed denial or denial, and (2) the right of the applicant to demand a hearing within twenty (20) days from the date of the notice (or a longer period if specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must state the specific deficiencies; applicants have a right to demand a hearing within the time specified in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing: publication timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When a hearing is required by the Act or this chapter, or the Commission finds a hearing is required in the public interest, the Secretary will issue a notice of hearing to be published in the Federal Register at least 15 days before the date set for hearing. For applications concerning limited work authorizations, construction permits, early site permits, or combined licenses for certain facility types or testing facilities, the notice must be published at least 30 days before the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For specified application types the notice must be issued as soon as practicable after the NRC has docketed the application.
